_doc: Every word the editor offers, colours and explains. 'group' is the semantic family a word belongs to; the directive groups also decide its colour. Prose is a port of contracts/stc/stc-contract.md — change it there first. tests/vocabulary.test.js holds the directive keys to the parser's DIRECTIVES.

source.summary: Open a picture and start a block of edits over it.
source.detail:
Opens a block. Everything indented under it applies to that picture. The spec is classified for whoever runs the script: `http(s)://…` is a URL, a path with `*`, `?` or `[` is a glob, one ending in `/` is a directory, anything else a single file. A glob or a directory runs the whole block once per file it matches.

Statements written *before* the first `@source` form the project block — they apply to whatever is already open, which on the command line means the `-i` input.

stencil.summary: Define a reusable block of directives.
stencil.detail:
The name is every word before the `:`, so `lines and rect` is one name. Parameters are positional — `@1`, `@2`, … — and the highest one you reference **is** the template's arity.

A template nothing calls is a warning, not an error.

use.summary: Set the default unit, set the shape style, or expand a template.
use.detail:
Three directives in one word:

- `@use cm` — bare numbers mean centimetres until the block ends.
- `@use line red, dashed, 3px` — the style every `@line` and `@rect` after it is drawn in.
- `@use stencil callout #ff3b30:` — expand a template here. Note the trailing colon.

crop.summary: Cut the picture down, by insets or by named edges.
crop.detail:
One value insets all four sides, two inset x then y, four read `x1 y1 x2 y2`. A leading `-` on a united value measures from the far edge, so `10%` becomes `x1=10% x2=-10%`.

The named form takes any of `x1`, `x2`, `y1`, `y2` and `aspect`. Mixing the two forms is an error.

filter.detail: Takes one of the five modes, or a colour — a colour makes a duotone in that hue. `none` clears a filter already applied.

line.summary: Draw an open polyline through two or more points.
line.detail:
A unit may attach to a component — `(14px, 50%)` — or to the pair after its `)`, as in `(56, 90)cm`, where it fills in only for components without one. Commas between points are optional.

The stroke comes from the `@use line` style in force.

rect.summary: Draw a closed shape; exactly two points are opposite corners.
rect.detail: A `@rect` is a `@line` that is closed, which is what lets it take a fill. Give it two points for a rectangle, or more for any closed polygon.

layout.summary: Draw a saved layout over the picture.
layout.detail: Reads a layout JSON — a grid, a set of guides, a frame — and draws it. `combine` (the default) keeps the marks already there; `replace` drops them first.

save.detail:
Bare, the CLI writes `<source-dir>/<base>-stencil.<ext>`. A target ending in `/` is a directory and gets the same generated name inside it; a bare name gets `<name>.<ext>` with the extension taken from the source; a full path is used verbatim.

In the editors a bare `@save` saves the open project, and `@save <name>` renames it first.

frame.summary: Pick a frame out of a video, and start a fresh set of edits.
frame.detail: Only where the surface can decode video — the CLI and the GUIs. Edit numbering restarts, so an `@undo` after a `@frame` cannot reach back past it. The saved base name becomes `<base>-frame-<n>`.

undo.detail:
Edits are numbered `1..n` as written, templates included, and are never renumbered.

- `@undo` — the last edit still live
- `@undo 3` — edit 3
- `@undo -1` — the last edit
- `@undo 1 2 -1` — each of those
- `@undo @line (1,1) (2,2)` — the last edit whose text matches

It is resolved when the script is compiled, not when it runs, so leaving an experiment in the file costs nothing.

redo.summary: Bring back the most recently undone edit.
redo.detail: With a count, repeats that many times.

contour.detail: Keeps the outlines and drops the flat areas.

none.detail: Clears a filter applied earlier in the block.

fill.summary: fill <colour> — the inside of closed shapes.
fill.detail: Only a `@rect`, or any closed shape, is filled. Use `transparent` to clear one.

point.summary: point <colour> <size> — the marker drawn at each point.

combine.summary: Keep the marks already on the picture.

x2.detail: A leading `-` measures from the right.

y2.detail: A leading `-` measures from the bottom.

aspect.detail: Combines with any edges you give; the rest are worked out.

%.summary: Per cent of the relevant axis.
%.detail: A leading `-` measures from the far end of that axis.
